The elemental powders were mixed in a V-type blender for 5h in argon atmosphere at room temperature.
The fully blended powders were compacted by cold isostatic pressing (CIP) method with pressure of 200 MPa for 5 min.
The green compacts were then sintered at 1300 ℃ for 4h in a high vacuum furnace, and followed by furnace-cooling.
the as-sintered billets were hot rolled (HR) on a hot-rolling mill. The rolling temperature was 950 ℃ and the total deformation was 80 %.
Finally, the hot-rolled alloys were subjected to annealing at 500 ℃ for 2 h in a muffle furnace.

the as-sintered alloy consists of a grey contrast α phase, a light contrast β phase and some residual pores with dark contrast. The rod-like primary α phases with a length of 20-50 µm and a width of 5-10 µm are surrounded by a small amount of β phases.
According to the statistics of software image-pro-plus-6, the volume fractions of α phase and β phase are 97 % and 3 %, respectively.
some residual pores with dark contrast
a duplex microstructure was observed, which consists of the α phase (dark area) and the transformed-β phase (light grey area).
Each of the transformed β grains is composed of several colonies and each colony consists of spaced α/β lamellas.

The high strength is mainly attributed to the precipitation strengthening of the silicide and the formation of fine-grained α′ phase.
indicates that ultra-fine α′ phase was obtained after hot rolling of P/M Ti-6Al-4Zr-0.5Mo-0.6Si alloy, which would be another positive effect on the mechanical properties.
It indicates that the fine and dispersed silicides may hinder the movement of dislocations in the matrix and play an important role to resist plastic deformation and improve the strength.
